title: narumi explicit minutes ensemble configuration and retry

ensemble_generator_id.description: Stable caller-generated UI/provenance identity for one generator, unique within the current ensemble. It is separate from label and array position and is excluded from semantic run/request identity. Changing only this ID must not create a run or external call.

ensemble_generator_label.description: Display-only label. Whitespace-only labels are rejected. Neither this label nor display order is sent in model prompts or used as a reason to generate again.

generators.description: Two to four configured generators. Implementations must also reject duplicate generator IDs even when labels or selections differ; JSON Schema uniqueItems alone does not enforce identity uniqueness. The same provider/connection with different models is allowed.

synthesizer.description: One explicitly selected text synthesis model. It may share a provider, connection and model with a generator; never infer an independent additional generation from shared/reused output.

minutes_ensemble_selection.description: Explicit text-only ensemble, mutually exclusive with minutes_model after the full config update is merged. Saving does not generate or send data. All generators, synthesizer and any API transcription selection must pass one transaction's policy/connection/model/runtime validation before execution, and each external call is revalidated. Reuse ModelSelection's closed provider parameters without changing legacy single-generation fingerprint or checkpoint semantics. API participants require explicit api_ok; policy is never promoted automatically. Execution concurrency is fixed at one. Semantic run identity is the multiset of resolver content scopes (provider, connection_id, model and effective content conditions; excluding connection_revision) with cache_epoch and deterministic duplicate ordinals, plus the synthesizer content scope. Generator ID, label and UI order are excluded. Changing only those excluded identities reuses the same run with zero provider sends, while current authorization/revision is still revalidated. For each packet, unique draft_chunk candidates are ordered by (draft_chunk content_projection_sha256, deterministic_duplicate_ordinal), then their canonical claim/question units are partitioned deterministically by the fixed unit and character limits; an empty document contributes one empty sentinel unit. Each resulting partition occurrence is one synthesizer chunk-leaf provider call. Its stable identity and order derive only from the packet window/content projection, the ordered candidate projections and duplicate ordinals, the exact ordered units, the fixed limits and the partition ordinal/hash, never opaque artifact/generator ID, label or UI order. Its current public input bindings are exactly that packet's source artifact plus each unique draft_chunk artifact that contributes a unit to the occurrence. The same source/draft_chunk pair may therefore appear in multiple leaf occurrences when one document is partitioned. The model-visible request may additionally contain only the fixed synthesis instructions and common brief; the request hash and content fingerprint also bind that request and the selected model content conditions. No wire request, hash, fingerprint or current input binding includes an aggregate draft artifact, another packet or a whole-run input merely to make publication reachability convenient. An unchanged packet, candidate content, common brief, limits and model conditions reproduce the same partition occurrences, leaf identities and downstream aggregation order when a different packet changes; only the changed packet's leaves and their downstream synthesis are invalidated.

minutes_ensemble.description: Nullable ensemble override. Omitted updates retain the saved value, null clears it, and an object replaces the whole configuration. A non-null minutes_model and non-null minutes_ensemble cannot coexist, including after partial updates. If both are null, retain the existing llm_provider path.

minutes_retry.description: One explicit retransmission confirmation for the current minutes-ensemble target and its unresolved unknown ancestry. The input run_id/node_id/call_id identify the current target that will receive the retransmission and need not belong to the run that owns blocked_attempt_id. blocked_attempt_id is the durable barrier cursor for that ancestry. Together these four IDs are the proof: the current target's three IDs plus the cursor attempt ID. One unresolved content fingerprint has exactly one durable public target. Recover origin as the first unknown attempt and expose it separately in read/error provenance. Require full expected_config with a non-null minutes_ensemble, force=false, and no transcription_retry. Compare current target membership, config and unknown receipt before sending, then consume this confirmation once when persisting the new pending attempt. Changing the target alone never consumes confirmation proof, reserves an attempt or sends provider data. Other unknown calls or stale attempt confirmations cannot reuse it. Increasing cache_epoch, creating another run or changing generator/connection identity never clears an unknown barrier. One content-unknown ancestry allows at most 64 lifetime attempts including its origin. Reject attempt 65 before consuming proof, reserving per-run budget or sending; preserve the barrier and expose a safe node error with reason=minutes_retry_limit_exceeded.

minutes_ensemble_limits.description: Application limits only. Execution also requires workflow.ensemble_generation and validated participant capabilities/authorization. Limits do not make a disabled transport executable. Attempt count accumulates across resume and confirmed retries in one run, excluding reused successes; it is not an exact HTTP-call count or a monetary ceiling.
